claims.text: High-throughput DFT can improve the accuracy of determining melting temperature, enthalpy and entropy of fusion, volume change upon melting, and liquid thermodynamic properties relative to current methods.
High-throughput DFT can improve the availability of melting and liquid-state thermodynamic data across a large compositional space.
High-throughput DFT can improve the efficiency of determining melting and liquid-state thermodynamic properties across a large compositional space.
Atomic-size mismatch acts as a structural mediator for the proposed improvement in melting and liquid-property prediction.
Shear-modulus mismatch acts as a structural mediator for the proposed improvement in melting and liquid-property prediction.
High-throughput DFT enables rapid screening of multicomponent alloys for single-phase solid-solution formation.
Single-phase solid-solution formation is governed by competition between the free energy of the solid solution and that of competing intermetallic phases.
The proposed intervention applies to both high-temperature solid and liquid states over a large multicomponent compositional space.
The choice of exchange-correlation functional may limit the accuracy of the DFT calculations.
Treatment of vibrational entropy may limit the accuracy of the DFT calculations.
Treatment of magnetic ordering may limit the accuracy of the DFT calculations.
Treatment of short-range ordering may limit the accuracy of the DFT calculations.
